trigger.Name: When to play
trigger.Hint: In PF2e, “Critical Success” is the degree of success (beating the DC by 10 counts), and “Natural 20” is the die face. Other systems go by the natural 20.

groupSkill.Name: Also on skill and Perception checks

groupFlat.Name: Also on flat checks and initiative

npc.Name: Also for NPCs
npc.Hint: Also play cut-ins for criticals by characters no player owns.

defaultTemplate.Name: Default template
defaultTemplate.Hint: Used when a character has no template of its own.

badgeText.Name: Natural 20 tag
badgeText.Hint: The small line above the headline on a natural 20. Leave it empty to show none. Each character can change or hide it in the editor.

soundPreset.Name: Default sound
soundPreset.Hint: Sounds 1–5 are synthesized by the module on the spot (no audio files). Choose “File” to use the file below.

fumbleEnabled.Name: Enable fumble cut-ins
fumbleEnabled.Hint: Also play a cut-in on a Critical Failure (or natural 1): the same template and picture in cold, faded colors, with a cracking screen and falling letters. Roll types and the NPC option follow the critical settings above.

fumbleTrigger.Name: Fumble — when to play
fumbleTrigger.Hint: In PF2e, “Critical Failure” is the degree of success (missing the DC by 10 counts), and “Natural 1” is the die face.

fumbleBadge.Name: Natural 1 tag
fumbleBadge.Hint: The small line shown on a natural 1. Leave it empty to show none.

fumbleSound.Name: Default fumble sound
fumbleSound.Hint: Fail sounds 1–3 are synthesized by the module too.

waitDice.Name: Play after Dice So Nice dice settle

landingShow.Name: Landing Page: Show on my screen
landingShow.Hint: When off, you see the map right away, even on a landing scene.

landingMotion.Name: Landing Page: Motion
landingMotion.Hint: Light rays, fog, embers and the slow push-in on the background. “Reduced” shows a still picture only.

stageSlots.Name: RP Stage: Characters on stage at once
stageSlots.Hint: 5 is recommended on wide screens only: the spots get narrower, pictures get smaller, and wide art (wings and the like) overlaps the next spot.

stageInset.Name: RP Stage: Screen margin (%)
stageInset.Hint: At 0 the whole screen is the stage. Otherwise the stage becomes a “scene window”, shrunk by that much on every side, with the darkened battle map around it. 5–8 recommended.

stageHold.Name: RP Stage: Hold the floor (seconds)
stageHold.Hint: For this long after speaking, a character can't be pushed off by a newcomer. While typing, their spot is always kept.

stageLeave.Name: RP Stage: Exit on their own after (seconds)
stageLeave.Hint: A character silent this long leaves the stage even if no one new speaks. At 0 they stay until their spot is needed.

stageFaceSeconds.Name: RP Stage: Expression duration (seconds)
stageFaceSeconds.Hint: “@smile” in a line goes back to the default face after this long (a little longer for long lines). “@@smile” stays until changed.

stageNarration.Name: RP Stage: GM narration
stageNarration.Hint: Lines written with the speaker bar's 🪶 (narration) appear in the dialogue box as narration, without a name plate.

stageLineSeconds.Name: RP Stage: Line fades after (seconds)
stageLineSeconds.Hint: The last line leaves the dialogue box after this long. At 0 it stays until the next line.

stageVoice.Name: RP Stage: Enter on voice (Discord) too
stageVoice.Hint: With a Discord voice bridge, whoever talks brings their character on stage (the one pinned on the bar, else their assigned character), just like typing. Also toggled with the bar's 🎙 button.

stageOwnedCast.Name: RP Stage: Players can speak as characters they own
stageOwnedCast.Hint: When off, players can only speak as the characters the GM gives them under “Speaking Rights”.

stageTypewriter.Name: RP Stage: Typewriter effect
stageTypewriter.Hint: Lines appear letter by letter (about 40 a second). When off, they appear all at once.

stagePause.Name: Pause the game during RP mode
stagePause.Hint: Pauses when RP mode turns on and unpauses when it turns off (a game that was already paused stays paused).

stageHidePause.Name: Hide the pause indicator during RP mode
stageHidePause.Hint: Hides the pause image and text in the middle of the screen (Alternative Pause Text included) and leaves only a small ⏸ in a corner of the stage.

stagePickBg.Name: Open the backdrop picker when RP mode turns on

stageLockView.Name: Lock players' view while a backdrop covers the map
stageLockView.Hint: While an RP backdrop is up, players can't pan or zoom the map or hover over tokens.

stageHideHud.Name: Hide party portraits and the turn tracker during the RP stage

stageShow.Name: Show the RP stage on my screen

speakerBar.Name: Speaker bar
speakerBar.Hint: A row of faces above the chat box. Click one to keep speaking as that character (clicking other tokens won't change it). Auto: shown to the GM in RP mode or when someone is on the bar, and to players with more than one character.

editor.Name: Per-character cut-ins
editor.Label: Open cut-in editor
editor.Hint: Set each character's picture, position, zoom, colors, line and sound. Also opens from the ⚡ button at the top of the character sheet.

landingEditor.Name: Landing Page
landingEditor.Label: Design landing page
landingEditor.Hint: Dress up the scene you are viewing as the campaign's title screen.

stageCast.Name: Serious RP Stage — Speaking Rights
stageCast.Label: Open speaking rights
stageCast.Hint: Turn serious RP mode on and off, and let players speak as characters they don't own (NPCs and others). Also in the “Rutz Toolkit” tab on the left.

stageBackdrop.Name: Serious RP Stage — Backdrop
stageBackdrop.Label: Choose backdrop
stageBackdrop.Hint: Keep backdrop pictures in folders and pick one. Also opens when RP mode turns on.

strike.Label: Strike — red slash · big letters
strike.Hint: A band slashing across the screen, halftone dots, a slanted portrait panel and letters that pop out.

band.Label: Emblem — wide band · light sweep
band.Hint: Black bars close in from above and below, the face slides into the band in the middle, then a gleam sweeps across.

eyes.Label: Eyeline — close-up strip on the eyes
eyes.Hint: A long, thin strip zoomed in on the eyes sweeps past. Line the position up with the eyes.

simple.Label: Simple — portrait · golden letters
simple.Hint: The portrait rises from below and the letters glow. The calmest of the looks.

cinematic.Label: Cinematic
cinematic.Hint: Letterbox bars, a slow push-in on the background, a big title low on the left

fantasy.Label: Dark Fantasy
fantasy.Hint: A dark gilded frame, a centered title and a column of buttons, portrait cards below

jrpg.Label: JRPG Title
jrpg.Hint: A bright logo, a menu on the right with a pointer, slanted party panels

silhouette.Label: Silhouette Party
silhouette.Hint: The party in a row in the dark — only the one under the mouse is lit

storybook.Label: Storybook
storybook.Hint: Title and menu on a parchment page, portraits pinned up like photographs

neon.Label: Cyber Neon
neon.Hint: A neon grid floor in the dark, a terminal menu, holographic ID cards

dossier.Label: Classified Dossier
dossier.Hint: A file folder on a desk, typewriter text and a red stamp, paper-clipped photos (great for CoC)

tarot.Label: Tarot & Stars
tarot.Hint: Tarot cards fanned out under a starry sky, a menu marked with stars

Cast.Title: RP Stage — Speaking Rights
Cast.OnHint: Start typing and that character steps onto the stage.
Cast.OffHint: Turning it on opens the RP stage on everyone's screen.
Cast.Players: Players — who they can speak as
Cast.OwnedNote: Dimmed chips are characters that player owns and can speak as automatically.
Cast.Help:
To hand them an NPC or anyone else, add it here (ownership stays as it is). You can also drop an actor from the sidebar onto a row. Players choose on the speaker bar above the chat box.
The GM needs nothing set up here: Alt+click a token or use the bar's + to put any character on the bar.
Cast.Limit: Each player can be given up to {n} characters.

Look.PickFirst: Pick a character on the speaker bar, or select a token, then open this.
Look.NotOwner: You don't have permission to change this character's stage settings.

Look.RefTip: Head height of a medium-sized character
Look.FacesHint: “@keyword” in a line → back to the default face after a few seconds; “@@keyword” → kept until changed. “@default” brings back the normal picture.
Look.Detected: Detected: {kind}{note}. The dotted line marks a medium-sized character's head height.

Look.DetectedFull: full body (feet just behind the dialogue box)
Look.NotMeasured: a picture from another site, so its margins can't be measured
